::: {#exr-miller-deriv-gaussian-kernel}
#### Derivative of the standard Gaussian kernel

Find the derivative of

$$f(x) = \exp{-\frac{x^2}{2}}$$
:::

::: {#sol-miller-deriv-gaussian-kernel}
Apply the chain rule (@thm-chain-rule) with outer function $\exp{u}$ and inner function $u(x) = -x^2/2$. Since $\dif{}{u}\exp{u} = \exp{u}$ (@thm-deriv-exp) and $u'(x) = -x$:

$$f'(x) = u'(x)\exp{u(x)} = -x\exp{-\frac{x^2}{2}}$$
:::
